learning_objective: 🎯 Refine your profits! Learn how to adjust final accounts for hidden, unpaid, or advance items to calculate the 100% accurate Net Profit based on the Accrual Concept.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Because of the 'Accrual Concept', we must record expenses and incomes for the CURRENT year, even if cash hasn't exchanged hands. Adjustments given outside the Trial Balance must be recorded in TWO places.
Outstanding Expense: An expense incurred but not yet paid (Add to expense, show as Liability). Prepaid Expense: An expense paid in advance for next year (Deduct from expense, show as Asset).
Accrued Income: Earned but not received (Add to income, show as Asset). Unearned Income: Received in advance but not yet earned (Deduct from income, show as Liability).

When a debtor runs away and doesn't pay, it's a Bad Debt (Loss). To be safe (Prudence principle), businesses also create a 'Provision for Doubtful Debts' for customers who MIGHT not pay in the future.

fun_activity.title: ✂️ The Timeline Cut
fun_activity.instructions: Draw a timeline from April 1 to March 31. You paid a 1-year insurance premium on Oct 1. Cut the timeline on March 31. The 6 months after March 31 are 'Prepaid'—you must subtract this amount from this year's profit!

exam_tips: 📌 Golden Rule: Any item INSIDE the Trial Balance has ONE effect. Any adjustment OUTSIDE the Trial Balance has TWO effects.
📌 For Provision for Doubtful Debts: New Provision is always calculated on Debtors AFTER deducting 'Further Bad Debts' given in adjustments.
📌 Manager's Commission 'On profit BEFORE charging such commission' = $Profit \times (Rate/100)$. If it says 'AFTER charging such commission' = $Profit \times (Rate / (100+Rate))$.
quick_recap: ⭐ Adjustments ensure that financial statements adhere strictly to the matching and accrual concepts.
⭐ Expenses related to the current year (paid or unpaid) must be matched against current revenues.
⭐ Creating provisions for doubtful debts is a direct application of the Prudence principle.
